authority.alpha_prerequisite: C-06 cannot close while immutable rrflowKV pages remain uncompressed, but a codec cannot enter the sole persistent substrate from candidate ratios alone. Research and bind the exact format, configuration, checksum, decode-bound, ownership, observability, failure, fixture, snapshot, fuzz, and DataFusion handoff changes before any production edit.

current_behavior: Segment v5 is the sole pre-release immutable format. It has an authenticated ordered MVCC spine, six 64-byte-aligned Arrow-layout page buffers, persisted row-group filters, physical/logical page lengths, page SHA-256 digests, bounded I/O, safe mapped ownership, and decoded-page cache/resource counters. Every page is nevertheless stored with plain encoding and compression none. The clean C-06i candidate corpus measured adaptive LZ4 and Zstandard but did not specify a production format, configuration path, allocation bound, corruption behavior, fixture replacement, or DataFusion ownership contract. Cache admission and value separation remain unintegrated candidates.
target_behavior: Create one cited, implementation-ready C-06i adaptive-page-compression plan. It must select or reject each measured codec and cache/value candidate; define a direct segment-v6 replacement with explicit writer policy and per-page codec identity; preserve raw-page mmap borrowing; require exact bounded allocation and decode for compressed pages; authenticate stored bytes before decode; account physical, logical, allocated, copied, borrowed, and decompressed bytes; enumerate every existing source, test, fixture, snapshot, fuzz, architecture, dependency, documentation, and evidence path; and state the exact incremental edit order and stop conditions. This package changes no runtime code or durable bytes and marks no roadmap gate complete.
unchanged_behavior: All rrflowKV production Rust, segment-v5 bytes, WAL/MVCC/manifest/compaction/snapshot semantics, filters, cache behavior, public types, dependencies, and fixtures remain unchanged in this research package.
DataFusion remains rrflowQL compute and consumes only stamped, bounded Arrow RecordBatches; it does not become persistence, transaction, decode, or cache authority.
The plan may adapt verified behavior from primary sources but may not copy an upstream format tree, public model, compatibility reader, hidden runtime, or fallback-on-missing-codec behavior.

Cache admission, Zstandard bottom-level placement, value separation, graph/BM25/vector/TurboQuant access paths, install/attunement, reasoning, SDKs, Connectome, binaries, and release qualification remain separate gates.
Product version remains 1.0.0; C-06 and POAM-002 remain open.
Only the private rrflow/rrflow-development repository may receive this pre-release planning package; official rrflow/rrflow remains untouched.

research.reason: Compression changes authenticated durable bytes, mapped ownership, allocation behavior, cache charge, corruption handling, snapshots, and the future DataFusion source contract. The existing candidate screen supplies RRFlow measurements but not these production semantics.

sources.title: LZ4 block format, pinned dev revision 0774d055
sources.retained_behavior: Use independent LZ4 blocks only because RRFlow page descriptors already carry compressed size and an authenticated bounded logical size; require safe bounded decoding and fuzzing.
sources.rejected_assumption: A raw LZ4 block is self-framing, self-bounding, or safe to decode before validating out-of-band lengths.

sources.title: lz4_flex 0.14.0 block implementation
sources.retained_behavior: Use caller-bounded block compression and decompress_into with safe encode, safe decode, and checked decode features.
sources.rejected_assumption: The size-prepended helper may control RRFlow allocation or unchecked/default feature selection is acceptable for persistent untrusted bytes.

sources.title: Apache Arrow columnar format 25.0.1
sources.retained_behavior: Keep each Arrow buffer independently selectable as raw when compression has insufficient benefit, and preserve 64-byte alignment for decoded buffers.
sources.rejected_assumption: Compressed Arrow-compatible storage pages remain zero-copy or RRFlow raw LZ4 blocks are Arrow IPC compressed messages.

sources.title: Apache Parquet page metadata and checksum contract
sources.retained_behavior: Carry distinct compressed and uncompressed page lengths and authenticate serialized stored page bytes after compression.
sources.rejected_assumption: A file-level digest eliminates the need for independently diagnosable page integrity and bounded page metadata.

sources.title: RocksDB compression guidance
sources.retained_behavior: Use lightweight LZ4 for the common path, leave incompressible blocks raw, and reserve heavier Zstandard policy for measured colder levels.
sources.rejected_assumption: RRFlow may silently fall back to no compression when a configured codec is unavailable or should copy RocksDB's per-level option model.

sources.title: RocksDB block-cache guidance
sources.retained_behavior: Charge decoded resident blocks, keep encoded bytes in the file/OS-cache domain, and qualify scan admission, pinning, and concurrency separately.
sources.rejected_assumption: A favorable segmented-LRU simulation proves a production cache replacement or cache capacity alone accounts for pinned iterator memory.

sources.title: Apache DataFusion custom table-provider guide
sources.retained_behavior: Keep planning lightweight and perform selective RRFlow I/O/decode in the execution stream, with pushdown only where rrflowKV avoids work.
sources.rejected_assumption: DataFusion owns RRFlow persistence, transactions, page decoding, or work performed during TableProvider planning.

sources.title: Apache DataFusion 55.0.0 MemoryPool contract
sources.retained_behavior: Retain separate rrflowKV source/decode/cache budgets because DataFusion does not automatically track DataSourceExec or flowing RecordBatch memory.
sources.rejected_assumption: Configuring a DataFusion MemoryPool automatically bounds decompression, page-cache residency, or source batches.

sources.title: Moka concurrent cache behavior
sources.retained_behavior: Retain TinyLFU as a later comparative admission reference only.
sources.rejected_assumption: Best-effort weighted capacity and a general cache library satisfy rrflowKV's exact decoded-byte, pinned-lifetime, scan, and storage-evidence contract.

runtime_trace.reason: The plan must bind future segment-write/open traces to policy identity and raw/compressed page counts/bytes, and future reads to physical, decoded, borrowed, allocated, copied, and decompressed counters.

resource_evidence.reason: The plan must reject decompression bombs before allocation, cap total logical page bytes, allocate exactly the authenticated logical length, and keep rrflowKV source/decode/cache accounting distinct from DataFusion MemoryPool accounting.

debugging_evidence.reason: The plan must enumerate codec/length/checksum corruption, threshold boundaries, raw-versus-compressed ownership, snapshot/reopen/compaction differential behavior, frozen vectors, fuzzing, and exact replay evidence.

first_failure_oracle: At baseline there is no C-06i adaptive-page-compression engineering-plan file and the roadmap index names only the completed candidate screen plus persisted-filter slice.
The current segment decoder rejects every compression byte other than zero and every current page records equal physical/logical lengths; the package must describe that fact without modifying it.

The candidate artifact proves byte and CPU observations for one corpus but contains no production segment-v6, allocation, corruption, snapshot, or DataFusion handoff proof; the research must not promote it beyond that scope.
Documentation validation must reject duplicate authority, broken warp points, rewritten historical evidence, missing exact file paths, or any readiness/completion claim.

stop_conditions: Any runtime Rust, Cargo dependency, lockfile, durable byte, fixture, test behavior, generated API surface, product version, or roadmap checkbox changes in this research package.
Any existing planned path lacks complete baseline review or a changed path is absent from this plan.
The plan leaves codec identity, threshold arithmetic, logical-size bounds, checksum order, decode ownership, evidence counters, direct format replacement, or failure tests unresolved.
The plan calls compression zero-copy, makes DataFusion a storage authority, silently introduces Moka/Zstandard/value separation, or copies an upstream format/API.
A push targets official origin, rewrites history, uses force, creates a tag/release, or is not immediately verified against development/main.
